summary:
Gorontalo stands under Indonesia's national framework. The source inventory records no ordinance, raid, protection measure, facility or support service specific to Gorontalo in either direction, so the national assessment applies.

Vigilante violence against transgender people is documented nationally: a wave of attacks on 14-16 July 2026 saw mobs attack trans women across the country, including more than 15 trans women in Bogor who were doused, stripped and beaten, with footage circulated online.

An October 2025 presidential decree lists "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among non-military threats alongside terrorism, radicalism and drug addiction, placing anti-LGBTQ policy inside national security framing.

Provincial moral laws and Aceh's caning regime remain in force; a researcher cited in August 2026 reporting documents markedly hardened anti-queer attitudes since 2016.

Legal gender change in Indonesia requires sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and the country provides no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Indonesia voted against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity in 2016, 2022 and 2025. A 2025 Pew survey found 93% of Indonesians rate homosexuality 'morally unacceptable'.
tangentialFactors:
Gorontalo is one of Indonesia's 38 provinces; the source inventory offers no comparative signal distinguishing it from other provinces on trans-specific enforcement, incidents or protection, so no inter-provincial ranking can be drawn.

The national pattern of vigilante attacks and official hostility documented in 2025-2026 reporting applies uniformly across provinces in the absence of provincial carve-outs.
localsOnly:
Indonesian residents seeking legal gender change must undergo sex-reassignment surgery and obtain judicial approval; no third-gender or X marker option exists.

No national law protects residents from discrimination or harassment on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Provincial moral provisions and Aceh's Sharia-based criminalisation remain part of the domestic legal landscape, though Aceh's regime is specific to that province and not to Gorontalo.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Gorontalo province has enacted its own moral ordinance, conducted local raids, or hosts any trans-specific support service is unresolved: the source inventory contains no Gorontalo-specific material in either direction.

The inventory does not resolve whether the 2022 penal-code extra-marital sex provision has been enforced through prosecution in Gorontalo.

Local violence-incident data for Gorontalo is not sourced; the July 2026 mob attacks cited here are documented for Bogor and other unspecified locations.
